title: Higher-order quantum thermodynamics: equilibrium and causal structure
summary: Quantum thermodynamics is traditionally formulated as a theory of equilibrium states and state transformations. Recent advances in higher-order quantum transformations, which describe physical scenarios beyond states and channels and provide a systematic framework for causal order, raise the question of how equilibrium should be defined and preserved in this more general setting. Starting from the Gibbs state as the unique equilibrium state, we identify equilibrium preservation as its natural higher-order extension.
